title: Counterfactual Traffic Synthesis and Stability Protocol for Eval Harness
author: Aisha Malik
content:
Summary:

This document defines a reproducible protocol and tooling approach for generating counterfactual and synthetic traffic to stress-test model serving and evaluation infrastructure. The protocol focuses on producing stable, explainable variations of live traffic for: 1) regression detection, 2) caching/kv-cache sensitivity tests, 3) quantization/precision shock tests, and 4) routing and fallback validation across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Why this exists:
- Live traffic is the gold standard but cannot always be replayed (privacy, PII, consent) or deterministically modified.
- Random synthetic traffic misses critical corner cases and distributional shifts.
- Counterfactual traffic (systematically altered real or simulated requests) bridges the gap: it preserves semantics while enabling controlled perturbations to probe failure modes.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied-ML engineers, SREs, model-onboarding owners, and QA.
- Scope: eval harness integrations (eval-mesh), synthetic traffic service (traffic-synth), and downstream triage runbooks.
- Excluded: labeling guidelines for human annotators (handled in prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).

Key definitions:
- Counterfactual Traffic: requests derived from canonical examples with targeted perturbations (e.g., role swaps, locale swaps, long-context insertion).
- Synthetic Shadow: traffic generated to imitate structural properties (token length, entity density) of a production route without using PII.
- Amplification Factor: multiplier applied to rare-slice traffic to increase statistical power when evaluating regressions.

High-level architecture:
- eval-mesh: orchestrates eval jobs and routes to target serving endpoints (hosted/dedicated/private).
- traffic-synth: independent microservice that composes counterfactuals and emits injections to eval-mesh or canary proxies.
- kv-cache-proxy: optional inline proxy to emulate and flush customer KV cache behaviors.
- quant-simulator: module that wraps model variants (float32->int8 quant) to compare outputs without changing live model binary.

Design principles:
- Determinism where possible: seeds + cataloged perturbation rules produce repeatable traffic.
- Observability-first: every synthetic request carries trace metadata (synth.catalog, perturbation.seed, amplification.id).
- Minimal fidelity loss: preserve original semantic intent of examples to avoid false positives.
- Safety and privacy: no PII copied from production; use token-level anonymization + synthetic named entities.

Catalog of perturbation families (examples):
1) Entity-level swaps: replace named entities with same-type synthetic tokens (e.g., COMPANY_X -> COMPANY_SYNTH).
2) Context elongation: insert benign long context passages to stress KV cache and long-context execution path.
3) Role inversion: flip question/answer framing to catch degenerative behavior in instruction-following models.
4) Locale and formatting: switch date/number formats, RTL language insertion, and timezone offsets.
5) Adversarial punctuation/noise: insert seldom-used unicode or tokenization traps.
6) Quantization stress: force sequences known to amplify FP error (dense numerical tables, alignment tokens).

Sampling strategies:
- Stratified-Aware Sampling: sample from production strata (route, customer-tier, model-version) proportionally, then amplify rare slices by Amplification Factor (AF).
- Edge-Amplify: identify slices with <1% frequency and apply AF 50–200x for statistical power.
- Counterfactual Pairs: always generate a (control, perturbed) pair to compute delta metrics per request.

Configuration table (recommended defaults):
Route/Workload Config YAML (example):
---
name: marketing-chat-route
seed_corpus: s3://eval-corpora/marketing-seed-v2.jsonl
perturbation_families: [entity_swaps, context_elongation, locale_swaps]
sample_strategy: stratified-aware
amplification_factors: {rare_slice: 100, default: 1}
batch_size: 128
duration: 2h
send_mode: shadow (no client-visible effects)
observe_metrics: [latency_p50, latency_p95, rsi, match_rate, token_delta]
---

CLI & examples:
- Generate a reproducible counterfactual run locally (dev):
$ traffic-synth run --config configs/marketing-chat-route.yaml --seed 42 --dry-run

- Push a 2-hour shadow stream to eval-mesh for canary:
$ traffic-synth run --config configs/marketing-chat-route.yaml --seed 20260214 --duration 2h --send-mode shadow --target eval-mesh:9090

- Quick curl to submit single counterfactual pair to eval-mesh (JSON):
curl -X POST https://eval-mesh.internal/api/v1/ingest -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"trace_id":"synth-0001","seed":123,"control":{"prompt":"Summarize quarterly results."},"perturbed":{"prompt":"Summarize quarterly results with extra accounting table appended."},"tags":{"family":"context_elongation","amplification":"1"}}'

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Response Stability Index (RSI): median absolute token-wise divergence between control and perturbed outputs. Alert if RSI > 0.12 for any amplified slice.
- Latency SLO regression: no more than +10% increase in route p95 latency under synthetic load vs baseline for burst sized up to batch_size*4.
- Semantic match_rate: fraction of perturbed outputs that preserve required intent labels (e.g., intent classification) — target > 0.92 for production promotion.
- Token delta: expected token increase per perturbation family; validate against a 3-sigma envelope built from historical runs.

Experiment / promotion checklist (canary procedure):
1) Local dry-run: run --dry-run and validate traces and perturbation coverage.
2) Shadow targeted canary (1% production RPS equivalent): send to eval-mesh -> observe metrics for 2h.
3) Amplified slice validation: for each rare slice with AF>1, ensure RSI < threshold and match_rate > 0.92.
4) Cross-model comparison: run quant-simulator variants (FP32 vs quant) on same stream and compute per-token delta; flag if > 0.08 for high-sensitivity routes.
5) Rollout decision: if all acceptance criteria pass, mark model as promotion-ready in onboarding matrix.
6) Post-promotion scan: run an overnight full-shaped synthetic sweep (AF=10 for rare slices) and collect stability artifacts.

Triage playbook (when synthetic run flags a regression):
1) Attach run metadata and open a regression issue with tag: eval:counterfactual. Include: config, seed, amplification id, and example (control, perturbed, model outputs).
2) Reproduce with same seed in dev environment. If non-deterministic, capture run logs and escalate to runtime team.
3) Bisect by perturbation family: run traffic-synth with single family enabled to isolate failure mode.
4) Run quant-simulator for quant regressions; if behavior diverges only in quant variant, escalate to model-ops + quant teams.
5) If divergence correlates with KV-cache eviction patterns, enable kv-cache-proxy with deterministic TTL=0/1 toggles to reproduce.
6) Document root cause, mitigations (e.g., prompt normalization, tokenizer glue fixes, caching TTL changes), and remediation timeline.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Traffic-synth: owned by applied-ml (oncall: applied-ml@redwood.internal) — SLA: 99.5% availability for dev runs.
- Eval-mesh ingestion: owned by eng-platform (oncall: eng-platform@redwood.internal) — SLA: 99.9% for evaluation ingestion.
- Triage and model promotion decisions: model-onboarding team.

Observability and artifacts to capture for every run:
- Trace ID list and sampling map (CSV).
- Per-request control/perturbed outputs (ndjson).
- Metric timeseries for RSI, latency percentiles, match_rate.
- Token-level diffs for top-k diverging examples.
- Run manifest (config + git sha + synth version).

Privacy & safety controls:
- No PII rule: any seed corpus coming from production must pass scrubbing + synthetic-entity-replacement before ingestion.
- Safety review checkpoint: any amplification >100x on slices with user-visible outputs requires a safety review from Research safety lead.

Appendix A — Example perturbation rule (JSON):
{
  "id": "entity_swap_company",
  "description": "Swap organization entities with synthetic names preserving token-length distribution.",
  "patterns": ["ORG", "COMPANY"],
  "replacement_pool": ["AcmeSyn", "BetaWorks", "NovaGrid"],
  "seeded": true
}

Appendix B — Common failure signatures and quick remediation:
- High RSI with low token delta: likely a model policy/decoding change. Remediation: check decoding params, temperature, and any soft-prompt patches.
- High token delta + latency spike: batching/backpressure interaction; remediate via batch tuning and autoscaling policy.
- Failures isolated to quant-simulator: investigate quant profile, re-run per-workload quant-tuner.
